description: Deliver supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql: an idempotent migration that makes the already-cached campaigns, applications, and platform_settings tables carry Jobs, Job Applications, and Banners data. Because these are ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN operations on relations already present in the PostgREST schema cache (not new CREATE TABLE relations), PostgREST continues to serve them and the PGRST205 problem does not recur. This feature is DB-only (a .sql file the user runs manually) and is independent of FEAT-002/003 but must land first so the column/mapping contract is fixed.
steps: Create supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql. Make it fully idempotent and safe to re-run.

Add the jobs marker + job-specific columns to campaigns: `ALTER TABLE public.campaigns ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_job boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;`. Reuse existing campaigns columns for the rest of the job fields (title, description, category, per_creator_payout, total_slots, deadline, cover_image_url, status) per context.json column_mapping - do NOT add duplicate columns for those.

Relax the campaigns.status CHECK constraint so job rows can use status 'closed' in addition to the existing values. Drop the existing check constraint if present and re-add a permissive one, e.g.: find the constraint via `ALTER TABLE public.campaigns DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS campaigns_status_check;` then `ALTER TABLE public.campaigns ADD CONSTRAINT campaigns_status_check CHECK (status IN ('draft','active','paused','completed','cancelled','closed'));`.

Add the job-application submission columns to applications (idempotent): `ALTER TABLE public.applications ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS submission_type text;` and similarly submission_url text, submission_note text, rejection_reason text, submitted_at timestamptz, reviewed_at timestamptz, reviewed_by uuid REFERENCES public.users(id).

Relax the applications.status CHECK so job-application status values 'applied' and 'submitted' are allowed in addition to the existing 'pending','approved','rejected','withdrawn': `ALTER TABLE public.applications DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS applications_status_check;` then re-add `CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','rejected','withdrawn','applied','submitted'))`.

Confirm/keep RLS working for the piggyback rows. campaigns already has: 'Anyone can read active campaigns' (status='active' OR brand_id=auth.uid() OR admin), 'Brands can create campaigns' (auth.uid()=brand_id), 'Brands can update own campaigns' (brand_id=auth.uid() OR admin). Since job rows are created by the admin with brand_id=admin.id, admins can create/read/update them and any 'active' job row is world-readable. Add a campaigns DELETE policy for admins if none exists (check supabase/add_campaign_delete_rls.sql for the existing pattern and reuse it; use DROP POLICY IF EXISTS before CREATE).

For applications: existing policies allow creator to insert/read/update own rows and admins to read/update all. Job applications use creator_id=user and are inserted/updated by that user, and admins review them, so existing policies suffice. Do NOT weaken campaign-application security. If an applications DELETE-by-admin policy is needed for deleteJob cascade behavior, note that job rows in campaigns cascade-delete their applications via the existing ON DELETE CASCADE FK (applications.campaign_id REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE) - so deleting the campaign row removes its applications automatically; no extra policy required.

platform_settings already has 'Anyone can read platform settings' (USING TRUE) and 'Admins can manage platform settings'. This is sufficient for banners-as-JSON: everyone can read the home_banners row, only admins can write it. Add no new policy.

Data migration (best-effort, guarded so it never errors if the source tables are absent): wrap in a DO $$ ... $$ block using a `to_regclass('public.jobs')` guard. If public.jobs exists, INSERT INTO campaigns the existing job rows mapping columns per context.json (brand_id := created_by, per_creator_payout := payment_amount, total_slots := COALESCE(max_slots, 1), is_job := true, keep the SAME id so existing job_applications still line up). Likewise if public.job_applications exists, INSERT INTO applications mapping job_id->campaign_id, user_id->creator_id, and the submission_* columns, keeping ids. Use ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING so re-runs are safe. If public.banners exists, aggregate its rows into a JSON array and UPSERT into platform_settings(key,value) VALUES ('home_banners', <json>) ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE. Every migration step must be null-safe and guarded so the script still succeeds when a legacy table is missing.
End the file with: `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';`

Add a top comment block explaining: this stores jobs inside campaigns (is_job=true), job applications inside applications, banners inside platform_settings key='home_banners', why (PGRST205 on new tables), and that it is safe to re-run.
acceptance_criteria: supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql exists and contains ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS for campaigns.is_job and for applications.submission_type/submission_url/submission_note/rejection_reason/submitted_at/reviewed_at/reviewed_by.
The file relaxes both the campaigns.status CHECK (adds 'closed') and applications.status CHECK (adds 'applied','submitted') using DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS then ADD CONSTRAINT.
The file contains NO `CREATE TABLE public.jobs`, `CREATE TABLE public.job_applications`, or `CREATE TABLE public.banners` (must not create the broken relations again).

Data-migration blocks are guarded with to_regclass so the script runs cleanly whether or not the legacy jobs/job_applications/banners tables still exist, and use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING/DO UPDATE for idempotency.
The file ends with NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
The file is idempotent: running it twice produces no errors.
verification: Read supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql end to end and confirm every ALTER uses IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS guards.
grep -n "CREATE TABLE" supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql returns nothing that creates jobs/job_applications/banners.
grep -n "NOTIFY pgrst" supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql matches the final line.
Confirm the status CHECK relaxations for both campaigns and applications are present.
findings: Created supabase/JOBS_VIA_CAMPAIGNS.sql (idempotent, DB-only deliverable the user runs manually in the Supabase SQL Editor). Verified reference facts against supabase/schema.sql: campaigns/applications/platform_settings definitions, default constraint names campaigns_status_check and applications_status_check, and applications.campaign_id REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (so deleting a job/campaign row cascade-deletes its applications, no extra applications DELETE policy needed). public.is_admin() SECURITY DEFINER helper exists (defined in fix_admin_rls.sql / clean_duplicate_policies.sql), so the reused admin DELETE policy for campaigns is valid. What the SQL does: (1) ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_job boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false on campaigns; (2) relax campaigns_status_check to add 'closed' (full list draft/active/paused/completed/cancelled/closed) via DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS then ADD; (3) ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS submission_type/submission_url/submission_note/rejection_reason text, submitted_at/reviewed_at timestamptz, reviewed_by uuid REFERENCES users(id) on applications; (4) relax applications_status_check to add 'applied','submitted' (full list pending/approved/rejected/withdrawn/applied/submitted); (5) admin DELETE policy on campaigns (DROP POLICY IF EXISTS then CREATE, USING public.is_admin()); no new policies on applications or platform_settings (existing ones suffice). (6) Guarded best-effort data migration in DO $$ blocks using to_regclass('public.jobs'/'public.job_applications'/'public.banners'): jobs->campaigns (brand_id:=created_by, per_creator_payout:=COALESCE(payment_amount,0), total_slots:=COALESCE(max_slots,0) [0=unlimited convention], is_job:=true, same id, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING); job_applications->applications (campaign_id:=job_id, creator_id:=user_id, copy submission_* + reviewed_*, created_at:=applied_at, same id, only where parent campaign row exists, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING); banners->platform_settings key='home_banners' as a JSON array (id/title/image_url/link_type/link_campaign_id/link_page/is_visible/sort_order/created_at/updated_at), ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE. (7) ends with NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';. NO CREATE TABLE for jobs/job_applications/banners. Verified via grep: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS, to_regclass, ON CONFLICT all present; no CREATE TABLE of the broken relations; NOTIFY pgrst is the final statement. Could NOT run psql/flutter/dart (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, not installed) - verification was read + grep only, per task constraints. REVIEW-FIX (2026-09-20-081332 issue #3): re-added server-side slot enforcement that regressed when jobs moved off the standalone job_applications table. Added an idempotent BEFORE INSERT trigger on public.applications (section 7, placed before the final NOTIFY): CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.enforce_job_slots() (SECURITY DEFINER, plpgsql) looks up the target campaign's is_job + total_slots; enforces ONLY when is_job IS TRUE AND total_slots IS NOT NULL AND total_slots > 0 (0/null = unlimited per the jobs convention), counting existing applications for that campaign_id with status IN ('applied','submitted','approved') and RAISE EXCEPTION 'This job has no slots remaining.' when count >= total_slots; real campaign applications (is_job=false/null) are never affected. DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS enforce_job_slots ON public.applications then CREATE TRIGGER keeps it idempotent/re-runnable. Null-safe: only enforces when total_slots is non-null and > 0. File still ends with NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'; (now section 8). Verified via grep: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION + DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS + CREATE TRIGGER + RAISE EXCEPTION present, trigger guarded on is_job, NOTIFY is the final statement.
